why: Rooms are connected components of non-wall cells, and one run cleans exactly one room. So the answer is the number of components that contain at least one '*': a flood fill per component.
hints: One run cleans a whole room, and it never helps to run twice in the same room. What do you really need to count?
Count connected components of non-'#' cells (4-directional) that contain at least one dirty '*' cell.
Scan the grid; from each unvisited '*' launch an iterative BFS/DFS over non-wall cells, marking them visited, and add 1. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: Rooms with only clean floor need no run; do not count every component.
With up to 200,000 cells, a recursive DFS will overflow Python's stack; use an explicit queue or stack.
A plan with no dirty cells at all returns 0.
